title: 1 Chronicles 6:66–81
context: 1 Chronicles 6:66–81 completes the Levitical city list for the rest of the Kohathites, the Gershonites, and the Merarites, again paralleling Joshua 21:20–40. Several names differ, such as Jokmeam where Joshua has Kibzaim, and Aner and Bileam where Joshua has Taanach and Gath Rimmon. Chronicles also does not name the tribe of Dan, and it lists Aijalon and Gath Rimmon in the Ephraim group, while Joshua 21:23–24 places them in Dan. These notes name the differences without harmonizing them. Both traditions see the Levites spread throughout Israel’s tribes as a sign that God’s worship and teaching were meant to reach the whole nation.

verses.text: Some of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of their borders out of the tribe of Ephraim.
verses.arminianNotes: Some Kohathite families had cities from the tribe of Ephraim. Arminians see the list returning to the rest of the Kohathites, now naming their cities, as in Joshua 21:20.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and read the verse as resuming the record after the summary. Both traditions see it as part of God’s provision for the Kohathites who were not priests.

verses.text: They gave to them the cities of refuge, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim with its pasture lands and Gezer with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: They received the cities of refuge, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer. Arminian readers note that Shechem was the city of refuge in this group (Joshua 21:21), a place with deep roots in Israel’s history.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and see the plural wording as a general description, as in 6:57. Both traditions read the verse as recording cities given to the Kohathites, without harmonizing the wording with Joshua.

verses.text: Jokmeam with its pasture lands, Beth Horon with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: Jokmeam and Beth Horon follow. Arminians note that Joshua 21:22 has Kibzaim where Chronicles has Jokmeam, and they name the difference without resolving it.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and leave the difference as it stands. Both traditions read the verse as part of the record of Kohathite cities in Ephraim.

verses.text: Aijalon with its pasture lands, Gath Rimmon with its pasture lands;
verses.arminianNotes: Aijalon and Gath Rimmon follow. Arminian readers note that Joshua 21:23–24 places these cities in the tribe of Dan, which Chronicles does not name in this list.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and name the difference without harmonizing it. Both traditions read the verse as continuing God’s provision for the Kohathite families.

verses.text: and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner with its pasture lands, and Bileam with its pasture lands, for the rest of the family of the sons of Kohath.
verses.arminianNotes: From the half-tribe of Manasseh come Aner and Bileam for the rest of the Kohathites. Arminians note that Joshua 21:25 has Taanach and Gath Rimmon, and they name the difference without resolving it.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and leave the names as they stand. Both traditions read the verse as completing the Kohathite city list.

verses.text: To the sons of Gershom were given, out of the family of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan with its pasture lands, and Ashtaroth with its pasture lands;
verses.arminianNotes: The Gershonites received Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth from the half-tribe of Manasseh. Arminian readers note that Golan was a city of refuge (Joshua 21:27) and that Joshua has Be Eshterah where Chronicles has Ashtaroth.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and name the difference without harmonizing it. Both traditions see God’s provision reaching the Gershonites east of the Jordan.

verses.text: and out of the tribe of Issachar, Kedesh with its pasture lands, Daberath with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: From Issachar come Kedesh and Daberath. Arminians note that Joshua 21:28 has Kishion where Chronicles has Kedesh, and they leave the difference unresolved.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and do not harmonize the lists. Both traditions read the verse as part of the record of Gershonite cities in the north.

verses.text: Ramoth with its pasture lands, and Anem with its pasture lands;
verses.arminianNotes: Ramoth and Anem follow. Arminian readers note that Joshua 21:29 has Jarmuth and En Gannim here, and they name the difference by reference.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and leave the names as they stand. Both traditions read the verse as continuing God’s provision for the Gershonite families in Issachar.

verses.text: and out of the tribe of Asher, Mashal with its pasture lands, Abdon with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: From Asher come Mashal and Abdon. Arminians note that Joshua 21:30 spells the first name Mishal, and they read the difference as a variation in the records without forcing agreement.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and name the difference by reference. Both traditions see the verse as part of the record placing Levites throughout Israel’s tribes.

verses.text: Hukok with its pasture lands, and Rehob with its pasture lands;
verses.arminianNotes: Hukok and Rehob follow. Arminian readers note that Joshua 21:31 has Helkath where Chronicles has Hukok, and they leave the difference unharmonized.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and name it by reference. Both traditions read the verse as completing the Gershonite cities in Asher.

verses.text: and out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee with its pasture lands, Hammon with its pasture lands, and Kiriathaim with its pasture lands.
verses.arminianNotes: From Naphtali come Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim. Arminians note that Kedesh was a city of refuge (Joshua 21:32) and that Joshua has Hammothdor and Kartan for the other two names.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and name the differences without harmonizing them. Both traditions read the verse as completing God’s provision for the Gershonites.

verses.text: To the rest of the Levites, the sons of Merari, were given, out of the tribe of Zebulun, Rimmono with its pasture lands, and Tabor with its pasture lands;
verses.arminianNotes: The Merarites received Rimmono and Tabor from Zebulun. Arminian readers note that Joshua 21:34–35 lists four different names, Jokneam, Kartah, Dimnah, and Nahalal, and they name the difference without resolving it.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and leave the lists as they stand. Both traditions read the verse as beginning the record of Merarite cities.

verses.text: and beyond the Jordan at Jericho, on the east side of the Jordan, were given them out of the tribe of Reuben: Bezer in the wilderness with its pasture lands, Jahzah with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: From Reuben, east of the Jordan at Jericho, come Bezer in the wilderness and Jahzah. Arminians note that Bezer was a city of refuge (Deuteronomy 4:43) and that Joshua 21:36 spells the second name Jahaz.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and name the spelling difference by reference. Both traditions see God’s provision reaching the Levites who lived in the tribes east of the Jordan.

verses.text: Kedemoth with its pasture lands, and Mephaath with its pasture lands;
verses.arminianNotes: Kedemoth and Mephaath follow. Arminian readers note that these names match Joshua 21:37, and they read the verse as part of a list that agrees in many places as well as differing in others.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and see the verse continuing the Reubenite cities. Both traditions treat it as shared ground about God’s provision for the Merarites.

verses.text: and out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with its pasture lands, Mahanaim with its pasture lands,
verses.arminianNotes: From Gad come Ramoth in Gilead and Mahanaim. Arminians note that Ramoth in Gilead was a city of refuge (Joshua 21:38) and that Mahanaim appears often in Israel’s history, including David’s flight from Absalom (2 Samuel 17:24).
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and see the cities matching the Joshua list here. Both traditions read the verse as part of God’s provision for the Levites in Gad.

verses.text: Heshbon with its pasture lands, and Jazer with its pasture lands.
verses.arminianNotes: Heshbon and Jazer complete the list. Arminian readers see the chapter ending with Levites settled throughout the land, so that God’s worship and teaching could be present among all the tribes.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree and note that these names match Joshua 21:39. Both traditions read the conclusion as testimony to God’s faithfulness in providing for those who served him, which is shared ground.
